cusa:ddi:1440.author: Nicolaus Cusanus
cusa:ddi:1440.work: De Docta Ignorantia Libri Tres (completed at Kues, February 12, 1440)
cusa:ddi:1440.locus: Dedicatio; Lib. I, Caps. 1–26; Lib. II, Caps. 1–13; Lib. III, Caps. 1–12; Epistola auctoris
cusa:ddi:1440.notes: Foundational treatise introducing learned ignorance, coincidence of opposites, infinite geometric figures, and the decentered moving Earth.

cusa:transmut:1445.author: Nicolaus Cusanus
cusa:transmut:1445.work: De Geometricis Transmutationibus, ad Paulum Dominici Florentinum (1445)
cusa:transmut:1445.notes: Introduces Cusa's compass-and-straightedge quarter-side sesquiquarta (5:4) rectification of the inscribed equilateral triangle, yielding pi_Cusa = 24*sqrt(21)/35.

cusa:compl:1453.author: Nicolaus Cusanus
cusa:compl:1453.work: De Mathematicis Complementis, ad Nicolaum V Pontificem Maximum (1453–1454)
cusa:compl:1453.notes: Written upon receiving Archimedes' Opera in Latin from Pope Nicholas V; develops the theory of prima linea (inradius) and secunda linea (circumradius) across isoperimetric polygons.

cusa:perf:1458.author: Nicolaus Cusanus
cusa:perf:1458.work: De Mathematica Perfectione, ad Antonium Cardinalem S. Chrysogoni (1458)
cusa:perf:1458.notes: Derives from the coincidence of minimal chord and minimal arc the fifth-order harmonic rectification hc : bc ~= 3*ac : (2*ac + ab).

cusa:aurea:1459.author: Nicolaus Cusanus
cusa:aurea:1459.work: R. D. N. Cardinalis S. Petri in Mathematicis Aurea Propositio (Rome, August 8, 1459)
cusa:aurea:1459.notes: Cusa's crowning three-ray formulation equating endpoint ascent and midpoint descent (theta ~= 3 sin theta / (2 + cos theta), residual theta^5/180).

cusa:paris:1514.author: Nicolaus Cusanus (ed. Jacques Lefèvre d'Étaples / Faber Stapulensis)
cusa:paris:1514.work: Haec accurata recognitio trium voluminum operum Clariss. P. Nicolai Cusae Cardinalis (Paris: Jodocus Badius Ascensius, 1514)
cusa:paris:1514.locus: Vol. I (De docta ignorantia); Vol. II, fols. 33r–114v (Mathematica)
cusa:paris:1514.notes: Monumental Renaissance humanist edition preserving full mathematical woodcuts and text witnesses prior to Rotta's 1913 omissions.

cusa:basel:1565.author: Nicolaus Cusanus
cusa:basel:1565.work: Nicolai de Cusa Cardinalis, utriusque iuris doctoris, in omnique philosophia incomparabilis viri, Opera, 3 vols. (Basel: Ex Officina Henricpetrina, August 1565)
cusa:basel:1565.notes: Standard early modern Basel edition read by Giordano Bruno, Johannes Kepler, and Willebrord Snellius.

cusa:rotta:1913.author: Nicolaus Cusanus (ed. Paolo Rotta)
cusa:rotta:1913.work: Nicolai Cusani De Docta Ignorantia Libri Tres (Bari: Gius. Laterza & Figli, Classici della Filosofia Moderna 19, 1913)
cusa:rotta:1913.notes: Early twentieth-century critical edition; McGill Library holds Raymond Klibansky's annotated copy recording Rotta's homeoteleuton omissions at p. 28 (I.13) and p. 31 (I.14).

cusa:heidelberg:1932.author: Nicolaus Cusanus (eds. Ernst Hoffmann & Raymond Klibansky)
cusa:heidelberg:1932.work: Nicolai de Cusa Opera Omnia, iussu et auctoritate Academiae Litterarum Heidelbergensis, Vol. I: De Docta Ignorantia (Leipzig: Felix Meiner, 1932)
cusa:heidelberg:1932.notes: Reference critical apparatus establishing the manuscript stemma (Codex Cusanus 218 et al.).

cusa:folkerts:2010.author: Nicolaus Cusanus (ed. Menso Folkerts)
cusa:folkerts:2010.work: Nicolai de Cusa Opera Omnia, Vol. XX: Scripta Mathematica (Hamburg: Felix Meiner, 2010)
cusa:folkerts:2010.notes: Definitive philological edition and mathematical analysis of Cusa's eleven mathematical treatises (1445–1459).

defelice:eos:2020.author: De Felice, Federica (ed.)
defelice:eos:2020.work: Niccolò Cusano: Scritti matematici (Berlin: Max Planck Institute for the History of Science, Edition Open Sources 13, 2020)
defelice:eos:2020.notes: Open-access edition preserving digital transcriptions and figures of Cusa's mathematical corpus.

hofmann:cusa:1952.author: Hofmann, Joseph Ehrenfried (trans. Josepha Hofmann)
hofmann:cusa:1952.work: Nikolaus von Cues: Die mathematischen Schriften (Hamburg: Felix Meiner, 1952; 2nd ed. 1979)
hofmann:cusa:1952.notes: Landmark modern mathematical reconstruction of Cusa's algebraic approximations and series expansions.

plato:opera.author: Plato
plato:opera.notes: Platonic foundations of recollection, mathematical dianoia vs. noesis, straight vs. round, and World-Soul harmony (geometor/plato).

aristotle:opera.author: Aristotle
aristotle:opera.work: Metaphysics II.1 (993b9), X.1 (1052b18); Physics VII.4 (248a10–b7); De Anima I.5 (411a5), II.3 (414b29); De Caelo II.13–14
aristotle:opera.notes: Aristotelian doctrines on the incomparability of straight and curved, unity as measure, and geocentric rest engaged and transformed by Cusa (geometor/aristotle).

euclid:elements.author: Euclid
euclid:elements.work: Elements, Books I, III, IV, VI & XII (ed. Heiberg; trans. Heath 1926)
euclid:elements.notes: Classical axiomatic baseline for Cusa's triangle, tangent, polygon-exhaustion, and quadrature arguments (geometor/euclid, geometor/elements).

archimedes:dimensio.author: Archimedes
archimedes:dimensio.work: Dimensio Circuli (Measurement of a Circle) & De Lineis Spiralibus (On Spirals)
archimedes:dimensio.locus: Dim. circ. Props. 1–3 (3+10/71 < pi < 3+1/7); Spir. Defs. & Prop. 18
archimedes:dimensio.notes: Primary ancient foil for Cusa's polygon bounds and critique of kinematic spiral rectification.

proclus:in-euclidem.author: Proclus Diadochus
proclus:in-euclidem.work: In Primum Euclidis Elementorum Librum Commentarii (ed. Friedlein 1873)
proclus:in-euclidem.notes: Neoplatonic philosophy of limit/unlimited, circular simplicity, and imaginative projection studied by Cusa (geometor/proclus).

dionysius:mystica.author: Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite
dionysius:mystica.work: De Mystica Theologia, De Divinis Nominibus, & Epistola I ad Gaium
dionysius:mystica.locus: MT I.1–3, V; DN I, V, XIII
dionysius:mystica.notes: Apophatic theological source explicitly cited in De docta ignorantia I.16–18.

aquinas:boethius.author: Thomas Aquinas
aquinas:boethius.work: Expositio super Librum Boethii de Trinitate, qq. 5–6
aquinas:boethius.notes: Scholastic account of mathematical abstraction and terminatio ad imaginationem (geometor/aquinas).

regiomontanus:quadratura:1533.author: Regiomontanus (Johannes Müller)
regiomontanus:quadratura:1533.work: De Quadratura Circuli Dialogus, Secundum Nicolaum Cusensem (composed 1464; Nuremberg: Johannes Petreius, 1533)
regiomontanus:quadratura:1533.notes: Demonstrated by Archimedean bounds that Cusa's 1450s rectifications slightly miss exact transcendental pi while honoring their ingenuity.

pacioli:divina:1509.author: Pacioli, Fra Luca
pacioli:divina:1509.notes: Parallels Cusa in treating irrational geometric proportion as an emblem of the incommensurable, triune Divine (geometor/pacioli).

durer:underweysung:1525.author: Dürer, Albrecht
durer:underweysung:1525.work: Underweysung der Messung, mit dem Zirckel und Richtscheyt (Nuremberg, 1525)
durer:underweysung:1525.notes: Applies constructive circle-quadrature and polygon transmutations in Northern Renaissance craft geometry.

kepler:mysterium:1596.author: Kepler, Johannes
kepler:mysterium:1596.work: Prodromus Dissertationum Cosmographicarum, continens Mysterium Cosmographicum (Tübingen, 1596) & Ad Vitellionem Paralipomena (1604)
kepler:mysterium:1596.locus: Myst. Cosm. Cap. II; Paralipomena Cap. IV.4
kepler:mysterium:1596.notes: Celebrates 'divinus mihi Cusanus' on curved/straight symbolism and extends Cusa's coincidence into the projective continuity of conic sections.

snellius:huygens:1654.author: Snellius, Willebrord & Huygens, Christiaan
snellius:huygens:1654.work: Cyclometricus (Leiden, 1621) & De Circuli Magnitudine Inventa (Leiden: Elzevier, 1654)
snellius:huygens:1654.notes: Rediscovers and rigorously proves the fifth-order Cusa–Snellius inequality 3 sin(theta)/(2 + cos theta) < theta.

casey:sequel:1886.author: Casey, John
casey:sequel:1886.work: A Sequel to the First Six Books of the Elements of Euclid, 4th ed. (Dublin: Hodges, Figgis & Co., 1886)
casey:sequel:1886.locus: Book VI, Section V (Theory of Inversion & Coaxal Circles)
casey:sequel:1886.notes: Synthetic theory of circle inversion and parabolic coaxial pencils formalizing Cusa's I.13 circle-line unity.

klein:elementary:1908.author: Klein, Felix
klein:elementary:1908.work: Elementarmathematik vom höheren Standpunkte aus, Bd. II: Geometrie (Leipzig: Teubner, 1908)
klein:elementary:1908.notes: Erlangen group-theoretic unification of lines and circles on the Riemann/Möbius sphere.

hoenen:noetica:1954.author: Hoenen, Petrus H. J., S.J.
hoenen:noetica:1954.work: De Noetica Geometriae: Origine Theoriae Cognitionis (Rome: Analecta Gregoriana 63, 1954)
hoenen:noetica:1954.notes: Epistemological study of insight into geometric necessity in concrete diagrams (geometor/hoenen).

wildberger:divine:2005.author: Wildberger, Norman J.
wildberger:divine:2005.work: Divine Proportions: Rational Trigonometry to Universal Geometry (Sydney: Wild Egg, 2005)
wildberger:divine:2005.locus: Chs. 3–6 (Quadrance, Spread, Triple Quad & Triple Spread Formulas)
wildberger:divine:2005.notes: Algebraic trigonometry proving pure rational convergence of Cusa's I.14 flattening triangle to collinearity (geometor/wildberger).
